title.en: Explosion offset reversibility against stored rest transforms

summary: Verify that an explosion scalar is a display offset over immutable rest transforms and that returning to zero restores them exactly.
objective: After exploding, isolating and returning the scalar to zero, every part matches its stored rest transform and inventory entry.
applies_when: An assembly separates parts for inspection and returns them to a rest pose.
Parts can also be isolated, selected or hidden while exploded.
Any panel reports assembly coordinates or dimensions while parts are separated.
intent_signals: parts do not return to their assembled position
check the exploded view is reversible
example_prompts: Check that this exploded speaker reassembles exactly.

principles: An explosion scalar is a display offset applied to an immutable rest transform; the rest transform is the record and the offset is a function of it.
Accumulating offsets onto the current transform loses the rest pose after the first pass, and setting the scalar back to zero cannot recover it.
Where the local matrix is composed from position, rotation and scale, repeated decompose and compose cycles drift; compare against the stored rest values, never against the previous frame.
implementation: Store each part rest transform once at load as position, quaternion and scale, and keep that copy read-only.
Drive display as the rest transform composed with an offset derived from the scalar and the authored explode axis, then set the scalar to 0, 1, 0, 0.5 and 0 in that order.

After the final zero, compare each part against the stored rest values as translation distance, rotation angle and scale ratio, since a decomposition may return the negated quaternion for the same rotation, and compare part count, IDs and material assignment against the load-time inventory.
Repeat the sequence with one part isolated and with a sub-assembly selected, since selection code is a common place where a transform is written back into the model.
observable_checks: Translation returns to rest within about one part in a million of the part bounding radius and rotation within a comparable angular margin; a residual that grows with the number of cycles identifies accumulation rather than rounding.
Part identity, count and material match the load-time inventory after isolation and reassembly.
Any coordinate or dimension reported while parts are separated is the rest coordinate, not the offset display coordinate.

known_limits: Checks transform bookkeeping only; it does not verify that the authored assembly is manufacturable or that parts could physically separate along those axes.
Authored verification guidance; no scene was run or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: In this scene graph the local transformation matrix is computed from the object position, rotation and scale, and is recomputed automatically unless the application takes over that update.
claims.scope: three.js Object3D transform behaviour; other engines define their own transform update rules.

source_refs.locator: position, quaternion, scale, matrix, matrixAutoUpdate and updateMatrix descriptions
